scope: Pre-registration of a 1080p p99 budget-crossing bracket at HEAD 466ff76. Diagnostic only; it does not replace the frozen capacity lower bound and does not constitute R3/R4 or production acceptance.

source.head: 466ff76a0b2a2f45b90280331bded77897ef6421
source.worktree: clean at registration; the ladder runs after the 2026-11-01 acceptance matrix finishes and each group registers whatever probe binary hash it actually observes

question: At HEAD 466ff76 on 1080p, between which two entity counts does the per-frame p99 first exceed the 240 FPS budget of 4.166667 ms, separately for render-only and for static update/extract/render?
why_this_is_worth_measuring: The frozen 2026-10-29 capacity verdict confirmed 1800 render-only and 1300 static as the highest sustained counts that passed and explicitly left the region above them untested: 1900 render-only, 1400 static and 1500 static failed, 1800 static was never measured.
On HEAD the frozen confirmed points still pass with more headroom and 1800 static also passes, so the frozen frontier is now strictly below the truth.
The 2026-10-31 40K verdict could only state a frontier transfer, not a crossing. A measured bracket replaces that with a real interval.
The ladder is cheap: three processes of twenty seconds per group, roughly ten minutes of machine time for the whole bracket.

predictions_recorded_before_measurement.note: Predictions exist so the ladder can falsify them. None of these numbers may be quoted as a result, and none may be called a measurement.

models.transfer_through_origin: p99(N) = k x N, so a cost ratio r at one point transfers the affordable entity count by 1/r. This is the model behind the two frontier-transfer numbers already published in the 2026-10-31 40K verdict.
models.affine_p99_fit: p99(N) = a + b x N fitted through two measured HEAD sustain points, i.e. it allows a fixed per-frame cost a.

transfer_through_origin.inputs: same-count ratio: frozen 1800 render-only p99 median 4.0939 ms vs HEAD 1800 render-only p99 median 3.2105 ms

affine_p99_fit.formula: p99(N) = 0.897 + 0.001285 x N  (ms, N in entities)
affine_p99_fit.inputs: HEAD sustain medians 1300 -> 2.5679 ms and 1800 -> 3.2105 ms

render_only.predicted_bracket_sources: 2400 and 2600 sit either side of the affine crossing; 2800 is included because the affine fit is itself an extrapolation from two low points.

transfer_through_origin.inputs: 40K-level ratio, because no frozen 1800-static sustain group existed; this mixes a same-scale ratio (render-only) with a 40K ratio (static)
transfer_through_origin.why_falsified: HEAD 1800 static passes at p99 3.7251 ms. A through-origin transfer that puts the frontier at 1782 is contradicted by a higher count passing, so the static curve has a fixed cost the through-origin model omits.

affine_p99_fit.formula: p99(N) = 1.371 + 0.001308 x N  (ms, N in entities)
affine_p99_fit.inputs: HEAD sustain medians 1300 -> 3.0710 ms and 1800 -> 3.7251 ms

static.predicted_bracket_sources: 2000, 2100, 2200, 2300 cover the affine crossing with one point of slack on each side plus one above.

ladder.note: Every point is a fresh run of three processes, twenty seconds each, 1920x1080, one fixed entity count, same process-per-group rule as the refresh sustain groups. run_40k_refresh.py always measures both modes at the entity count it is given, so each run yields one render-only point and one static point at that count; the extra cross points are reported as a grid rather than discarded. No point is re-sampled; if a run is invalid the ladder is reported with the gap.

per_mode_expected_bracket.render-only: 2400 (pass expected) to 2600 (fail expected), 2800 as the confirming upper point

anchor_1800.purpose: Rebuild-drift anchor. The refresh measured 1800 render-only p99 median 3.2105 ms and 1800 static p99 median 3.7251 ms with probe binary 91ed0d303c09ef92e6abab9e30b63c87da77322d1dc7132c6b45204c220578b9, which the matrix --clean-first rebuilds destroyed. Re-measuring 1800 inside the new build separates a build effect from a scale effect.
anchor_1800.rule: If the ladder's 1800 medians differ from 3.2105 / 3.7251 ms by more than the ladder's own repeatability, every ladder number is reported as belonging to its own build and no cross-build delta is claimed. If they agree within that band, the ladder may be described as reproducing the refresh sustain points.

ladder.order_reason: Interleaved and ascending/descending alternately so a machine-level drift over the twenty minutes cannot masquerade as a scale effect.

pass_criteria.per_process: the runner's own rule, exactly: no validity problem, wall FPS >= 240, cycle p99 <= 4166.666666666667 us, and every complete one-second window >= 240 frames. This is the capacity definition used by the frozen 2026-10-29 groups and by the refresh sustain groups; a handful of individual frames over budget does not fail a process (the frozen 1300 static group passed with 24 over-budget frames in one process), so the individual over-budget count is reported as information only, never used to flip a pass.
pass_criteria.repeatability: the per-group relative range of p99 and of wall FPS is reported but does not gate the bracket; a range above 15% is recorded as a caveat and the group is used only for pass/fail, never as a speed reading

decision_rule.bracketed: Report [P, F): the largest passing count P and the smallest failing count above it, provided no count below P failed and no count above F passed.
decision_rule.non_monotonic: If the ladder is non-monotonic (a higher count passes while a lower one fails), report every point and state that the frontier is not bracketed. Do not smooth, average or interpolate.
decision_rule.never: Never publish a single crossing number, never interpolate between points, and never overwrite the frozen 2026-10-29 confirmed list.

artifacts.per_group: registration.json, results.json, three per-process frame logs
